dedupe_keys.name: wind waterway infrastructure data of the german federal waterways wsv web map service

description: WInD (Wasserstraßen-Infrastrukturdaten) is the Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration's inventory of the structures on Germany's federal waterways, published as a web map service run by ITZBund for federal and state authorities and the public. Coverage is all federal waterways in Germany. It describes and identifies each object and is organised in the administration's asset classes: objects for water discharge and navigability (river bed, canal bridges, navigation tunnels, groynes, training walls), for regulating water levels and gauging (weirs, storm surge barriers, water level stations), for shipping (ship locks, ship lifts, boat locks, lock control centres, passing and turning places, berths, transhipment points, ports), for aids to navigation, for crossing traffic (rail and road bridges, pipe and cable bridges, overhead lines, ferries, tunnels and culverts) and for other duties; the capabilities list 172 classes. The WMS 1.3.0 service is free with no fees or access constraints, and all 206 layers are queryable, returning attributes as XML or JSON through GetFeatureInfo. Caveats: there is no bulk download or WFS in this service, attribute content is only seen per query, no update date is given, and the WSV page describing WInD returned 404. The inventory supports network and capacity studies of inland navigation, such as locating locks, bridges and weirs that limit vessel size or fail in floods and low water; related records are the Inland ENCs and the Rhine-Alpine inland freight data.
